scenario.fault_family: BGP config error (wrong remote-as on a neighbor)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Since a config push this morning, the BGP session between
spine_router_0_1 and leaf_router_0_1 will not come up: it cycles
without ever reaching Established, and the leaf's log shows its OPEN
being rejected by the spine with an AS error. Every other session in
the fabric is Established, all interfaces are UP, and users report at
most a brief blip -- pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) still
reach each other. Find the fault.

injection.action: misconfigure the remote-as of the leaf_router_0_1 neighbor

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: spine_router_0_1 BGP neighbor remote-as
Mechanism: spine_router_0_1 (AS 65101) peers with leaf_router_0_1 at
  172.16.0.11, whose real AS is 65201. The neighbor statement was
  changed to `remote-as 65999`, so when the leaf's OPEN arrives
  announcing AS 65201, spine_router_0_1 rejects it with an OPEN error
  (Bad Peer AS) notification and the session can never establish --
  it cycles between Idle/Active/OpenSent. The CLOS fabric is
  redundant: leaf_router_0_1 still peers with spine_router_0_0, so
  both host prefixes stay reachable and the impact is loss of the
  second spine path for leaf_router_0_1, not an outage.
Localization: spine_router_0_1 (the misconfigured side; leaf_router_0_1's
  own config is unchanged and correct)
Root cause: neighbor 172.16.0.11 configured with remote-as 65999
  instead of 65201 on spine_router_0_1
Fix: set the neighbor's remote-as back to 65201 on spine_router_0_1
  (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
Correct the remote-as on spine_router_0_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router bgp 65101"
 -c "neighbor 172.16.0.11 remote-as 65201"`
Note: the injection changed only the running config; the intended
config is still intact in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so `service frr restart`
on spine_router_0_1 is an equally correct fix.

must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only the spine_router_0_1 <-> leaf_router_0_1 session is affected while links are UP and all other sessions are Established
bonus-cites-mismatch-values: cites the configured remote-as 65999 vs leaf_router_0_1's actual AS 65201
bonus-exonerates-leaf: notes leaf_router_0_1's own configuration is correct/unchanged, so the misconfiguration is on the spine side

agent.diagnosis_text:
The failing BGP session is between spine_router_0_1 (AS 65101, eth2
172.16.0.10/31) and leaf_router_0_1 (AS 65201, eth1 172.16.0.11/31).
The interface link is fully UP on both sides, so connectivity is not
the issue.

The fault is a wrong remote-as value in spine_router_0_1's BGP
configuration. Its running config declares "neighbor 172.16.0.11
remote-as 65999", but leaf_router_0_1's actual local AS number is
65201. When leaf_router_0_1 sends its BGP OPEN message advertising
AS 65201, spine_router_0_1 compares that value against the expected
65999, finds a mismatch, and immediately sends a BGP NOTIFICATION
with Error Code 2 (OPEN Message Error) Subcode 2 (Bad Peer AS). This
causes the session to reset, which is exactly the "AS error" the leaf
log reports. The session then retries, producing the rapid
Idle/Connect churn visible in the high message counts (16 sent by the
spine, 13 by the leaf) and the non-zero Up/Down timer cycling every
~30 seconds. All other sessions (spine_router_0_1 → super_spine,
spine_router_0_1 → leaf_router_0_0) carry the correct remote-as
values and are Established.

Root cause: a bad config push introduced the wrong peer AS number
(65999 instead of 65201) for leaf_router_0_1 on spine_router_0_1.

Corrective fix: on spine_router_0_1, replace "neighbor 172.16.0.11
remote-as 65999" with "neighbor 172.16.0.11 remote-as 65201". The
session will immediately reach Established after the next retry.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly names spine_router_0_1 as the misconfigured device (wrong remote-as configured for neighbor 172.16.0.11).

per_axis.rationale: States the problem is a wrong remote-as on spine_router_0_1 (configured 65999 while the peer's AS is 65201).

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: only the spine_router_0_1 <-> leaf_router_0_1 session is affected while links are UP and all other sessions are Established
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly isolates the failing session between spine_router_0_1 and leaf_router_0_1, notes interfaces are UP, and confirms all other sessions from spine_router_0_1 are Established.

per_axis.axis: bonus-cites-mismatch-values: cites the configured remote-as 65999 vs leaf_router_0_1's actual AS 65201
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states the spine is configured with remote-as 65999 while the leaf's AS is 65201, identifying the mismatch.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-leaf: notes leaf_router_0_1's own configuration is correct/unchanged, so the misconfiguration is on the spine side
per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly states leaf_router_0_1 is AS 65201 and that spine_router_0_1 is configured with the incorrect remote-as (65999), attributing the fault to the spine and leaving the leaf's config correct/unchanged.
The agent explicitly instructs changing the neighbor remote-as on spine_router_0_1 to 65201, which matches the expected fix (or equivalently restarting FRR since the intended config is in frr.conf).

Investigation ran configs, interface and BGP summaries on both routers and the conclusions follow logically from the observed AS numbers, interface state, and BGP session behavior; the only minor gap is the investigation log excerpts are truncated and do not explicitly show the exact misconfigured remote-as line or the BGP NOTIFICATION payload, though the agent ran the relevant commands and recorded those findings.
